In ACDT 95, see https://github.com/ethereum/pm/issues/2209#issuecomment-5568033889, @jochem-brouwer floated the idea of shipping [EIP-8253](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8253) in Glamsterdam, as a companion/addition EIP of EIP-7928 and an alternative solution to [EIP-7610](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8253) (now DFI'd).

- Jochem posted a TLDR of his motivation here: https://gist.github.com/jochem-brouwer/72b97452ba440da909e5da5bdf876817 
- The solution involves bumping the nonce in 28 inactive accounts and (post Glamsterdam) updating a block's BAL.
- Client teams in [ACDT 95](https://forkcast.org/calls/acdt/095) were torn: They agreed that while it would be a nice clean-up; it is very late in the fork dev process for this addition.
- Would postponing EIP-8253 until Hegota incur more techncial debt than necessary? 

The final decision was deferred to ACDE.

We are asking to PFI [EIP-8411](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12299) (fast execution payload broadcast) for Hegota, replacing the previously PFIed [EIP-8142](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12072/) (Blocks in blobs).

Rationale and context:
* As Glamsterdam increases gas limits and EIP-8198 PFIed for Hegota proposes reducing slot duration, efficient payload propagation is critical to prevent empty slots and reorgs. Standard gossipsub is increasingly inefficient for these large messages.
* While EIP-8142 aimed to leverage data column subnets for payload broadcast, concerns were raised regarding KZG proving on the builder's critical path and the complexities of subnet reuse.
* The EIP-8411 proposes simpler approach: **chunked** payload broadcast on a dedicated gossipsub topic with Merkle root commitment

For why chunking the payload improves its broadcast you can read in this post by Csaba ([link](https://ethresear.ch/t/wen-fast-payload-broadcast-segment-code-push-pull-and-everything-in-between/25913))

We understand that we are proposing a new EIP after the PFI deadline (August 6th), which is why we are asking for ACD decision on whether to include it in the Hegota PFI list nonetheless
Nethermind Client team Hegota scoping: https://gist.github.com/LukaszRozmej/9fc6b743bb82e363e16a0337bfc0bbc9 EL: CL:

I am asking that https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7979, Call and Return Opcodes for the EVM, be Considered for Inclusion.  It is a _very_ small, _very_ long-standing, _very_ important ask that I and others have put _many_ years of work into.

One data structure -- a stack.  Three instructions -- a no-op, a push, and a pop.  Repeatedly proposed, implemented, tested, and very nearly shipped in various forms over the years.

At this point I am the only remaining co-author.  I am 72 and in bad health.  Martin and Brooke have moved on.  Max died at 71.  I can't keep waiting forever.

> We are asking to PFI EIP-8411 (fast execution payload broadcast) for Hegota, replacing the previously PFIed EIP-8142 (Blocks in blobs).

It looks to me like EIP-8411 is CL side, so then the decision whether to allow the post deadline PFI is for ACDC next week. I will by default not put it on the agenda for today. Let me know if you disagree!

> It looks to me like EIP-8411 is CL side, so then the decision whether to allow the post deadline PFI is for ACDC next week. I will by default not put it on the agenda for today. Let me know if you disagree!

I agree this is more CL side (in fact the EIP-8411 does not imply and EL changes at all). 
May I ask to have it as the last agenda item, not to steal time from EL discussions.

If CL decision can only be made on the ACDC call, then I only bring this up to attention and then we can have a more extensive discussions next week
Asking to bump priority for EIP-8360. It's clearly necessary and glamsterdam introduced a breaking change.

_Here is a short explainer on the role of EIP-8372, and why we should CFI it together with EIP-8368 for now (published also [here](https://x.com/weboftrees/status/2098027937777713256?s=20))._ Think of a parcel truck. It can be full in two ways, too heavy or out of room, so parcel companies charge you for whichever is bigger: what your box actually weighs or a "pretend weight" they assign based on its size. A pillow in a big box weighs almost nothing but gets charged as if it were heavy. Now imagine the booking system uses the truck's weight limit for both actual and pretend weight. Suppose better tires and bridges mean the trucks can carry twice as much weight, but they are still the same size. Since the weight limit doubles, all the pretend weights have to be doubled too, otherwise you are selling room that isn't there. This is what EIP-8368 does when the gas limit goes up (state is the room, execution is the weight, CPSB sets the pretend weight). However, we cannot tell for sure how customers will react to higher pretend weights for pillows and toilet paper. They may mostly ship dense things like computers, leaving room unused. Or they may keep sending bulky items, leaving much of the weight allowance unused. We will have a better hunch after Glamsterdam. Under the shared limit we cannot fix this by adjusting the pretend weights further, since that would also change how much room we sell. EIP-8372 separates the pretend weight limit from the actual weight limit, so we can change what we charge for room without changing how much room we allow. We can then use what we have learned about demand to aim for a better balance between space and weight. We should therefore keep both EIP-8368 and EIP-8372 CFI until we have observed actual usage patterns after "pretend weights" (CPSB) rise in Glamsterdam.

Lido contributors' view on EL EIPs [shared in Magicians thread](https://ethereum-magicians.org/t/eip-8081-hegota-network-upgrade-meta-thread/26876/9) .

We encourage all teams posting their positions there, so that there is an official thread were all opinions are transparently posted.
This meeting occurred more than 24 hours ago. Closing automatically.
